### With COVID-19 in the rear-view mirror, how are in-person events supporting the battery industry?

Did you know there were over 100 lithium-related events last year? We launched a global lithium events calendar in 2023 to keep track of them all and shared it with our stakeholders on our website. This year, 【71†we are tracking even more events†lithium.org】, and you can add them all to your calendar with a click of the mouse!

It would have been a full-time job to attend all the lithium events last year, but we did manage to attend over 20 and give presentations at most of those. Our own events schedule grew nicely, too. We hosted in-person networking events in Salta, Argentina; Perth, Australia; London, United Kingdom; and Las Vegas, United States. This was in addition to our regular series of webinars exclusively for members covering the lithium market and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues.

### How has lithium demand evolved over the last 12 months? Are there any emerging trends, and are we on track to meet approaching climate targets?

The short answer is that lithium demand continued to show double-digit growth last year, driven by the transition to green transport. 【40†Electric vehicle (EV)】 sales in 2023 reached 【72†14 million units†www.ev-volumes.com】, representing 34% growth over 2022.

Like any significant industrial policy, the energy transition faces challenges; however, momentum is building, and regulatory support is growing.

The growing use of lithium batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) is also noteworthy. ESS play a key role in meeting net zero targets, storing energy from different sources and discharging it when needed. ESS help to balance the electric grid, provide backup power, and improve grid stability, which is important when an increasing percentage of electricity comes from intermittent renewable sources.

[Image 3]© shutterstock/Quality Stock Arts

### Are there any challenges in the supply chain for lithium batteries that have surfaced recently, and what steps are being taken to mitigate these challenges?

Education is a perennial challenge because of the rapid growth in the social and economic importance of lithium. As recently as five years ago, politicians rarely mentioned lithium, but now it has become a hot topic with all the media attention and regulatory interest this brings. We are seeing a real thirst for reliable information about lithium from industry, regulators, and the public.

On a more practical level, a key challenge is the time needed to bring on new industrial lithium mines. This is far longer than the time needed to build a refinery or EV factory, even up to ten years. We often hear from our members that the bottleneck is the time taken to secure permission, and it is encouraging to see several countries looking very closely at their legislative framework with regard to encouraging faster development of lithium mines without sacrificing the quality of the process.

### ILiA and its members all champion sustainability in the industry. Are there any emerging practices that are helping to ensure this further?

Yes, that is correct. In fact, sustainability is one of ILiA’s three core principles and was one of the key considerations for the founding members when they created ILiA in 2021. We support our members’ efforts to supply lithium that is sustainably and responsibly sourced through workshops, webinars, and the work of our technical subcommittees.

Many lithium companies are adopting standards that certify their performance. There are many mining standards which can apply to the lithium industry, and ILiA does not endorse a particular one, but it is worth recognising that last year, two of our Core Members, Albemarle Corporation and SQM, achieved the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) standard, which is considered by many people in the industry to be the hardest mining standard to achieve.

### What is ILiA working on to support its members in achieving sustainability?

One of our flagship projects, run by the Sustainable Lithium Subcommittee, is the creation of standardised guidance on how to measure the product environmental footprint of carbon and water used in lithium mining and refining. This will have a major impact, we hope, in streamlining how lithium life cycle assessments (LCAs) are done. The standardised guidance will be clear, concise, and accessible to producers, suppliers, LCA practitioners, authorities, and academia. Our goal is for lithium LCAs to truly represent the industry and contain reliable and comparable information.

It is of critical importance for the lithium industry as it will serve to create a benchmark by which the industry can measure its greenhouse gas credentials. It will be available on the ILiA website for download.

For this project, we created a global multi-stakeholder team of members and non-members under the leadership of Mark De Boer from Albemarle Corporation. The first chapter focuses on the carbon footprint of lithium and will be published in the first quarter of 2024. The second chapter will examine the water footprint of the lithium industry and will be published in the second half of 2024. Both projects are open to the public, and anyone interested in joining should contact us.

### What regulatory or policy changes have affected the lithium market in the past year, and how have industry players adapted to these changes?

The last year was something of a watershed for the lithium industry, with several major regulations and legislations hitting their stride. For example, in November 2023, the European Union reached a provisional agreement on the Critical Raw Materials Act, which aims to increase and diversify the EU’s critical raw materials supply, strengthen circularity and recycling and boost research and innovation on resource efficiency.

US and Canadian lithium sector development could still forge ahead in 2024 with the potential startup of new construction projects to provide much-needed domestic supply, despite pricing and demand headwinds that weighed on the global industry this year.

As 2023 ends, market participants in the key north Asia market are reporting ongoing weakness for spot lithium activity amid bearish sentiment and falling prices,【113† S&P Global Commodity Insights reported earlier†platform.platts.spglobal.com】. There have been very few inquiries from traders and scarce transactions, according to a Chinese producer.

"Overseas are cutting their orders because they cannot use up the amount they purchased under long-term contract," said a second Chinese producer.

However, soft market trends should be expected in the burgeoning lithium industry, and long-term fundamentals remain strong, according to Rahul Sen Sharma, president and co-CEO of Indxx.

"When you're talking about these big disruptive transformational changes, oftentimes you have problems and other types of issues that come up because you're trying to change so much so quickly," Sen Sharma told S&P Global. "This is normal, and I don't think it should be unexpected."

Indxx provides indexing solutions for ETFs and offers some products focused on the battery material sector.

Bullish sentiment for the lithium and battery sectors is also evident in Quebec, which has been investing heavily to establish the complete supply chain within the province, from mining to electric vehicle production.

"The demand will be there, whatever happens, because we need to electrify our cars," Jean-François Béland, vice president of Ressources Québec, said in an interview.

Ressources Québec, a unit of Investissement Québec (IQ), is working to foster investment in the province's energy and natural resources sectors.

"Lithium and critical minerals are, in the 21st century, what coal was in the 19th century and what oil was in the 20th century," Béland added.

### Incoming projects

Since 2020, the fallouts from the pandemic and various geopolitical events have strained international supply chains and led to record-high commodity prices. At the same time, governments globally have introduced waves of policy initiatives promoting energy transition, industrial onshoring and regional supply chains.

### With COVID-19 in the rear-view mirror, how are in-person events supporting the battery industry?

Did you know there were over 100 lithium-related events last year? We launched a global lithium events calendar in 2023 to keep track of them all and shared it with our stakeholders on our website. This year, 【71†we are tracking even more events†lithium.org】, and you can add them all to your calendar with a click of the mouse!

It would have been a full-time job to attend all the lithium events last year, but we did manage to attend over 20 and give presentations at most of those. Our own events schedule grew nicely, too. We hosted in-person networking events in Salta, Argentina; Perth, Australia; London, United Kingdom; and Las Vegas, United States. This was in addition to our regular series of webinars exclusively for members covering the lithium market and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues.

### How has lithium demand evolved over the last 12 months? Are there any emerging trends, and are we on track to meet approaching climate targets?

The short answer is that lithium demand continued to show double-digit growth last year, driven by the transition to green transport. 【40†Electric vehicle (EV)】 sales in 2023 reached 【72†14 million units†www.ev-volumes.com】, representing 34% growth over 2022.

Like any significant industrial policy, the energy transition faces challenges; however, momentum is building, and regulatory support is growing.

The growing use of lithium batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) is also noteworthy. ESS play a key role in meeting net zero targets, storing energy from different sources and discharging it when needed. ESS help to balance the electric grid, provide backup power, and improve grid stability, which is important when an increasing percentage of electricity comes from intermittent renewable sources.

[Image 3]© shutterstock/Quality Stock Arts

### Are there any challenges in the supply chain for lithium batteries that have surfaced recently, and what steps are being taken to mitigate these challenges?

Education is a perennial challenge because of the rapid growth in the social and economic importance of lithium. As recently as five years ago, politicians rarely mentioned lithium, but now it has become a hot topic with all the media attention and regulatory interest this brings. We are seeing a real thirst for reliable information about lithium from industry, regulators, and the public.

On a more practical level, a key challenge is the time needed to bring on new industrial lithium mines. This is far longer than the time needed to build a refinery or EV factory, even up to ten years. We often hear from our members that the bottleneck is the time taken to secure permission, and it is encouraging to see several countries looking very closely at their legislative framework with regard to encouraging faster development of lithium mines without sacrificing the quality of the process.

### ILiA and its members all champion sustainability in the industry. Are there any emerging practices that are helping to ensure this further?

Yes, that is correct. In fact, sustainability is one of ILiA’s three core principles and was one of the key considerations for the founding members when they created ILiA in 2021. We support our members’ efforts to supply lithium that is sustainably and responsibly sourced through workshops, webinars, and the work of our technical subcommittees.

Many lithium companies are adopting standards that certify their performance. There are many mining standards which can apply to the lithium industry, and ILiA does not endorse a particular one, but it is worth recognising that last year, two of our Core Members, Albemarle Corporation and SQM, achieved the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) standard, which is considered by many people in the industry to be the hardest mining standard to achieve.

### What is ILiA working on to support its members in achieving sustainability?

One of our flagship projects, run by the Sustainable Lithium Subcommittee, is the creation of standardised guidance on how to measure the product environmental footprint of carbon and water used in lithium mining and refining. This will have a major impact, we hope, in streamlining how lithium life cycle assessments (LCAs) are done. The standardised guidance will be clear, concise, and accessible to producers, suppliers, LCA practitioners, authorities, and academia. Our goal is for lithium LCAs to truly represent the industry and contain reliable and comparable information.

It is of critical importance for the lithium industry as it will serve to create a benchmark by which the industry can measure its greenhouse gas credentials. It will be available on the ILiA website for download.

For this project, we created a global multi-stakeholder team of members and non-members under the leadership of Mark De Boer from Albemarle Corporation. The first chapter focuses on the carbon footprint of lithium and will be published in the first quarter of 2024. The second chapter will examine the water footprint of the lithium industry and will be published in the second half of 2024. Both projects are open to the public, and anyone interested in joining should contact us.

### What regulatory or policy changes have affected the lithium market in the past year, and how have industry players adapted to these changes?

The last year was something of a watershed for the lithium industry, with several major regulations and legislations hitting their stride. For example, in November 2023, the European Union reached a provisional agreement on the Critical Raw Materials Act, which aims to increase and diversify the EU’s critical raw materials supply, strengthen circularity and recycling and boost research and innovation on resource efficiency.

Another key theme in regulatory developments is battery recycling. The battery in an EV can be recycled repeatedly, creating a circular ec

### By Application Analysis

Batteries to Hold Major Share owing to the Growing Demand from Consumer Electronics

On the basis of application, the market is segmented into batteries, glass & 【48†ceramics】, lubricant, polymers, metallurgy, medical, air treatment, and others.

The batteries segment accounted for a major market share in 2023 and will likely continue its dominance during the forecast timeframe. LIBs are used in many combinations of active materials for the cathode, electrolyte, and anode. They are either primary or secondary batteries. Primary batteries are used in cameras, calculators, electronic games, watches, computers, and other devices. In contrast, secondary batteries are used in portable computers, telephones, tablets, electric vehicles, cordless tools, and video cameras.

A surge in electric vehicle sales due to rise in per capita disposable income and user preferences will drive the LIB market. The demand for rechargeable batteries declined due to the coronavirus outbreak, thus contributing to the downfall of the automotive industry. As per the BloombergNEF forecast, battery consignments to carmakers fell by about 14% in 2020. Thus, consumer awareness and a major mind shift toward low-cost transportation will drive market growth in the coming years.

Metal carbonate is used to lower the temperature and thermal expansion in glass and ceramics applications. It is used in glass-ceramics cooktops to reduce thermal expansion, ensure color consistency, increase mold strength, improve durability, lower viscosity, and increase melt rate. SCHOTT AG specializes in manufacturing glass and glass-ceramics and uses a lithium aluminium silicate system to produce glass-ceramics, such as CERAN cooktop panels, ZERODUR glass-ceramic fire protection glasses and security, and ROBAX fire viewing windows for fireplaces.

### By End-User Analysis

The Automotive Industry Dominates the Market Due to a Growing Preference for Hybrid and Electric Vehicles

On the basis of end-user, the market is segmented into automotive, 【50†consumer electronics】, industrial, energy storage, and others.

The automobile industry is currently dominated by fossil fuel consumption but is increasingly moving toward becoming an alternate source of energy, such as lithium-ion-backed battery technology. The increasing demand for EVs and the shift toward clean energy will drive the product demand in the coming years. For instance, the Indian Government launched FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles) along with national & state-level regulations to make 30% of electric cars target by 2030 by adding 450 GW of renewable sources by establishing 34 GW/136 GW of battery storage requirements to make the country a major user of LIB.

The consumer electronics segment has grown exponentially in recent times. LIBs are used under rechargeable gadgets to store the proper energy-to-weight ratios and high open-circuit voltage. The advancement in battery technology is making electronic products more refined and slim, which makes higher use of batteries to increase the running time of products. In addition, these batteries have a high power density for more battery life in a lighter package. Hence, an increase in demand for 【51†smartphones】 and consumer electronics is expected to drive market growth.

## REGIONAL INSIGHTS

Asia Pacific Lithium Market Size, 2023 (USD Billion)

To get more information on the regional analysis of this market, 【52† Request a Free sample 】 

Asia Pacific is estimated to hold the largest lithium market share, owing to widespread product usage in the industrial and commercial sectors, including power, consumer electronics, chemical, industrial, general manufacturing, and others. Asia Pacific is rapidly developing due to various government initiatives and increasing foreign investments in the industrial sector. The easy availability of raw materials is considered one factor supporting the market growth.

Additionally, the presence of a large number of lithium and its derivatives-producing companies in emerging countries such as India, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and China is surging the product demand. China is one of the largest producers of electronic components such as fuel cells, batteries, and capacitors. There has been advancement in fuel cell technologies for electric vehicles to aid the rules set by the government to reduce the pollution that occurs due to the burning of petrochemicals and gasoline.

To know how our report can help streamline your business, 【49† Speak to Analyst 】 

The market in North America is likely to rise considerably during the lithium market forecast period. The increasing adoption of cleaner energy sources due to stringent regulatory rules is surging regional growth. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has various schemes and funding programs that support the usage of green and sustainable sources of energy like solar, wind, geothermal, and others. The increasing adoption of 【53†solar panels】 has created a substantial demand for cells and batteries to store energy.

For instance, in a technology transfer program of NASA, the gas-powered engines of aircraft were replaced by LIB packs designed by NASA and other contractor partnerships. These factors will contribute to the growth of the market in North America.

Europe has witnessed significant industrial development in the last decade. The increasing investment of the European Union for R&D in automobile, ICT, and healthcare sectors is the main factor driving the market growth. According to the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA), Europe's battery electric vehicles hold 12.1% of the total market share, compared to 9.1%in 2021 or 1.9%in 2019.

Latin America accounts for around 70% of the world’s lithium reserves, where the metal is used in rechargeable batteries for EVs and mobile phones. Chile produces metals that are cheap and high-quality. Chile’s government is allowing new entrants as the region's market is consolidated in nature.

It would have been a full-time job to attend all the lithium events last year, but we did manage to attend over 20 and give presentations at most of those. Our own events schedule grew nicely, too. We hosted in-person networking events in Salta, Argentina; Perth, Australia; London, United Kingdom; and Las Vegas, United States. This was in addition to our regular series of webinars exclusively for members covering the lithium market and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues.

### How has lithium demand evolved over the last 12 months? Are there any emerging trends, and are we on track to meet approaching climate targets?

The short answer is that lithium demand continued to show double-digit growth last year, driven by the transition to green transport. 【40†Electric vehicle (EV)】 sales in 2023 reached 【72†14 million units†www.ev-volumes.com】, representing 34% growth over 2022.

Like any significant industrial policy, the energy transition faces challenges; however, momentum is building, and regulatory support is growing.

The growing use of lithium batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) is also noteworthy. ESS play a key role in meeting net zero targets, storing energy from different sources and discharging it when needed. ESS help to balance the electric grid, provide backup power, and improve grid stability, which is important when an increasing percentage of electricity comes from intermittent renewable sources.

[Image 3]© shutterstock/Quality Stock Arts

### Are there any challenges in the supply chain for lithium batteries that have surfaced recently, and what steps are being taken to mitigate these challenges?

Education is a perennial challenge because of the rapid growth in the social and economic importance of lithium. As recently as five years ago, politicians rarely mentioned lithium, but now it has become a hot topic with all the media attention and regulatory interest this brings. We are seeing a real thirst for reliable information about lithium from industry, regulators, and the public.

On a more practical level, a key challenge is the time needed to bring on new industrial lithium mines. This is far longer than the time needed to build a refinery or EV factory, even up to ten years. We often hear from our members that the bottleneck is the time taken to secure permission, and it is encouraging to see several countries looking very closely at their legislative framework with regard to encouraging faster development of lithium mines without sacrificing the quality of the process.

### ILiA and its members all champion sustainability in the industry. Are there any emerging practices that are helping to ensure this further?

Yes, that is correct. In fact, sustainability is one of ILiA’s three core principles and was one of the key considerations for the founding members when they created ILiA in 2021. We support our members’ efforts to supply lithium that is sustainably and responsibly sourced through workshops, webinars, and the work of our technical subcommittees.

Many lithium companies are adopting standards that certify their performance. There are many mining standards which can apply to the lithium industry, and ILiA does not endorse a particular one, but it is worth recognising that last year, two of our Core Members, Albemarle Corporation and SQM, achieved the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) standard, which is considered by many people in the industry to be the hardest mining standard to achieve.

### What is ILiA working on to support its members in achieving sustainability?

One of our flagship projects, run by the Sustainable Lithium Subcommittee, is the creation of standardised guidance on how to measure the product environmental footprint of carbon and water used in lithium mining and refining. This will have a major impact, we hope, in streamlining how lithium life cycle assessments (LCAs) are done. The standardised guidance will be clear, concise, and accessible to producers, suppliers, LCA practitioners, authorities, and academia. Our goal is for lithium LCAs to truly represent the industry and contain reliable and comparable information.

It is of critical importance for the lithium industry as it will serve to create a benchmark by which the industry can measure its greenhouse gas credentials. It will be available on the ILiA website for download.

For this project, we created a global multi-stakeholder team of members and non-members under the leadership of Mark De Boer from Albemarle Corporation. The first chapter focuses on the carbon footprint of lithium and will be published in the first quarter of 2024. The second chapter will examine the water footprint of the lithium industry and will be published in the second half of 2024. ### With COVID-19 in the rear-view mirror, how are in-person events supporting the battery industry?

Did you know there were over 100 lithium-related events last year? We launched a global lithium events calendar in 2023 to keep track of them all and shared it with our stakeholders on our website. This year, 【71†we are tracking even more events†lithium.org】, and you can add them all to your calendar with a click of the mouse!

It would have been a full-time job to attend all the lithium events last year, but we did manage to attend over 20 and give presentations at most of those. Our own events schedule grew nicely, too. We hosted in-person networking events in Salta, Argentina; Perth, Australia; London, United Kingdom; and Las Vegas, United States. This was in addition to our regular series of webinars exclusively for members covering the lithium market and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues.

### How has lithium demand evolved over the last 12 months? Are there any emerging trends, and are we on track to meet approaching climate targets?

The short answer is that lithium demand continued to show double-digit growth last year, driven by the transition to green transport. 【40†Electric vehicle (EV)】 sales in 2023 reached 【72†14 million units†www.ev-volumes.com】, representing 34% growth over 2022.

Like any significant industrial policy, the energy transition faces challenges; however, momentum is building, and regulatory support is growing.

The growing use of lithium batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) is also noteworthy. ESS play a key role in meeting net zero targets, storing energy from different sources and discharging it when needed. ESS help to balance the electric grid, provide backup power, and improve grid stability, which is important when an increasing percentage of electricity comes from intermittent renewable sources.

[Image 3]© shutterstock/Quality Stock Arts

### Are there any challenges in the supply chain for lithium batteries that have surfaced recently, and what steps are being taken to mitigate these challenges?

Education is a perennial challenge because of the rapid growth in the social and economic importance of lithium. As recently as five years ago, politicians rarely mentioned lithium, but now it has become a hot topic with all the media attention and regulatory interest this brings. We are seeing a real thirst for reliable information about lithium from industry, regulators, and the public.

On a more practical level, a key challenge is the time needed to bring on new industrial lithium mines. This is far longer than the time needed to build a refinery or EV factory, even up to ten years. We often hear from our members that the bottleneck is the time taken to secure permission, and it is encouraging to see several countries looking very closely at their legislative framework with regard to encouraging faster development of lithium mines without sacrificing the quality of the process.

### ILiA and its members all champion sustainability in the industry. Are there any emerging practices that are helping to ensure this further?

Yes, that is correct. In fact, sustainability is one of ILiA’s three core principles and was one of the key considerations for the founding members when they created ILiA in 2021. We support our members’ efforts to supply lithium that is sustainably and responsibly sourced through workshops, webinars, and the work of our technical subcommittees.

Many lithium companies are adopting standards that certify their performance. There are many mining standards which can apply to the lithium industry, and ILiA does not endorse a particular one, but it is worth recognising that last year, two of our Core Members, Albemarle Corporation and SQM, achieved the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) standard, which is considered by many people in the industry to be the hardest mining standard to achieve.

### What is ILiA working on to support its members in achieving sustainability?

One of our flagship projects, run by the Sustainable Lithium Subcommittee, is the creation of standardised guidance on how to measure the product environmental footprint of carbon and water used in lithium mining and refining. This will have a major impact, we hope, in streamlining how lithium life cycle assessments (LCAs) are done. The standardised guidance will be clear, concise, and accessible to producers, suppliers, LCA practitioners, authorities, and academia. Our goal is for lithium LCAs to truly represent the industry and contain reliable and comparable information.

It is of critical importance for the lithium industry as it will serve to create a benchmark by which the industry can measure its greenhouse gas credentials. It will be available on the ILiA website for download.

For this project, we created a global multi-stakeholder team of members and non-members under the leadership of Mark De Boer from Albemarle Corporation. The first chapter focuses on the carbon footprint of lithium and will be published in the first quarter of 2024. The second chapter will examine the water footprint of the lithium industry and will be published in the second half of 2024. Both projects are open to the public, and anyone interested in joining should contact us.

### What regulatory or policy changes have affected the lithium market in the past year, and how have industry players adapted to these changes?

The last year was something of a watershed for the lithium industry, with several major regulations and legislations hitting their stride. For example, in November 2023, the European Union reached a provisional agreement on the Critical Raw Materials Act, which aims to increase and diversify the EU’s critical raw materials supply, strengthen circularity and recycling and boost research and innovation on resource efficiency.

Another key theme in regulatory developments is battery recycling. The battery in an EV can be recycled repeatedly, creating a circular ec

It uses various methods, such as electrodialysis, ion exchange, and adsorption, to extract lithium ions directly from brine or other lithium-rich solutions. India's lithium resources and production are relatively small compared to global leaders. Here's an overview:

### Lithium Resources in India:
- **Estimated Resources**: India has recently discovered significant lithium resources in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir, with an estimated 5.9 million metric tons of inferred resources. However, these are still in the exploration phase and not classified as reserves yet.

### Lithium Production and Usage in India:
- **Cumulative Production**: India does not have significant historical lithium production. Most of India's lithium demand is met through imports.
- **Annual Consumption**: India's annual lithium consumption has been increasing, driven by the growing demand for electric vehicles and renewable energy storage. However, precise consumption figures are not as readily available but are estimated to be a small fraction of global consumption.

### Summary:
- **Total Estimated Lithium Resources in India**: 5.9 million metric tons (inferred resources)
- **Lithium Used in India**: Minimal domestic production; most lithium used is imported.

India is in the early stages of exploring and potentially developing its lithium resources. The significant recent discovery in Jammu and Kashmir could position India as a more substantial player in the global lithium market in the future.

Estimates regarding the percentage of lithium present in the world versus how much has been used are based on known reserves, resources, and historical production data. Here's an overview:

### Global Lithium Reserves and Resources:
- **Global Lithium Reserves**: As of recent estimates, the world’s lithium reserves are approximately 21 million metric tons. Reserves are the part of the resource base that can be economically extracted with current technology.
- **Global Lithium Resources**: Lithium resources are estimated to be around 86 million metric tons. Resources include reserves as well as deposits that are not currently economically viable or fully explored.

### Lithium Production and Usage:
- **Cumulative Production**: Since large-scale lithium mining began in the mid-20th century, approximately 4 million metric tons of lithium have been produced and used.
- **Annual Production**: In recent years, global lithium production has been increasing, with annual production reaching about 100,000 to 120,000 metric tons of lithium content.

### Percentage Estimates:
- **Used Lithium**: If we consider the cumulative production of about 4 million metric tons, this represents roughly 4.7% of the estimated total lithium resources (86 million metric tons).
- **Remaining Reserves**: The remaining reserves of 21 million metric tons represent approximately 24% of the total estimated lithium resources.

### Summary:
- **Total Estimated Lithium Resources**: 86 million metric tons
- **Global Lithium Reserves**: 21 million metric tons
- **Lithium Used (Cumulative Production)**: 4 million metric tons

Given these numbers, approximately 4.7% of the world's total estimated lithium resources have been used to date. The remaining resources are yet to be fully exploited, with a significant portion still available for future use.

Lithium deposits are created through geological processes that concentrate lithium-bearing minerals and brines. There are two primary types of lithium deposits:

1. **Pegmatite Deposits**:
   - **Formation**: These deposits are formed from the cooling of magma. As the magma cools, it crystallizes, and certain elements, including lithium, become concentrated in the last remaining fluid. This fluid forms pegmatites, which are coarse-grained igneous rocks.
   - **Lithium Minerals**: The most common lithium-bearing minerals found in pegmatites are spodumene, lepidolite, and petalite.

2. **Brine Deposits**:
   - **Formation**: These deposits are typically found in closed-basin salt flats, also known as salars. Over long periods, lithium is leached from volcanic rocks by weathering and is carried by water into these basins. As water evaporates, it leaves behind concentrated lithium brines.
   - **Location**: These are often found in arid regions, such as the "Lithium Triangle" in South America, which includes parts of Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile.

**Other Types**:
- **Clay Deposits**: Lithium can also be found in certain clay minerals, such as hectorite. These deposits are formed from the alteration of volcanic ash in alkaline lake environments.

In summary, lithium deposits are created through the concentration of lithium in pegmatites formed by magma cooling and in brines from the evaporation of lithium-rich water in closed basins.

### Future Potential of the Lithium Sector:

The lithium sector has strong future potential due to the increasing demand for electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy storage, and portable electronics. As countries and industries shift towards cleaner energy and sustainable technologies, the demand for lithium is expected to grow significantly.

### Opportunities for You in the Lithium Sector:

Given your background in product management, technology development, and a keen interest in national growth, there are several ways you can benefit from the burgeoning lithium sector in India:

1. **Technology and Innovation**:
   - **Develop Lithium-Related Technologies**: Leverage your expertise in developing applications to create innovative solutions for lithium extraction, refining, and battery manufacturing. This could include software for optimizing mining operations or developing advanced battery management systems.
   - **3D Modeling and Simulation**: Use your skills in 3D modeling tools like Blender and Houdini to create simulations and models for lithium mining operations, equipment design, and processing plants.

2. **Product Management**:
   - **Lead Projects in Lithium Processing**: Manage projects focused on establishing lithium extraction and processing facilities. Your experience in compliance solutions can help navigate the regulatory landscape.
   - **Develop SaaS Solutions for Mining Operations**: Create software solutions to streamline operations, manage logistics, and ensure compliance in the lithium mining sector.

3. **Education and Training**:
   - **Develop Training Programs**: Create educational programs and training modules for personnel in the lithium industry, focusing on best practices, technology use, and safety protocols. This could align with your family's educational enterprise.
   - **Promote Awareness and Knowledge Sharing**: Organize workshops, seminars, and conferences to promote awareness and knowledge sharing about the lithium sector.

4. **Business Development**:
   - **Forge Strategic Partnerships**: Collaborate with international lithium companies to bring advanced technologies and expertise to India. Establish partnerships for joint ventures and knowledge transfer.
   - **Investment and Funding**: Identify investment opportunities in the lithium sector and work with financial institutions to secure funding for promising projects.

5. **Sustainability and CSR**:
   - **Promote Sustainable Practices**: Advocate for and implement sustainable mining practices. Use your platform to ensure that environmental and social governance (ESG) standards are met.
   - **Community Engagement**: Engage with local communities to ensure that lithium mining and production benefit local populations and address any concerns they may have.

### Action Plan:

1. **Research and Networking**:
   - Stay updated with the latest trends and developments in the lithium sector.
   - Network with industry experts, attend conferences, and participate in relevant forums.

2. **Skill Enhancement**:
   - Gain knowledge in lithium extraction technologies, battery manufacturing, and renewable energy storage.
   - Consider certifications or courses related to mining, energy storage, and project management.

3. **Strategic Initiatives**:
   - Identify potential projects and areas where you can apply your expertise.
   - Develop a business plan for entering the lithium sector, focusing on innovation, sustainability, and strategic partnerships.

By leveraging your diverse skills and experience, you can position yourself to take advantage of the growth and opportunities in the lithium sector, contributing to both your personal growth and the development of the industry in India.

US and Canadian lithium sector development could still forge ahead in 2024 with the potential startup of new construction projects to provide much-needed domestic supply, despite pricing and demand headwinds that weighed on the global industry this year.

###### Not registered?

Receive daily email alerts, subscriber notes & personalize your experience. 

【112† Register Now 】 

As 2023 ends, market participants in the key north Asia market are reporting ongoing weakness for spot lithium activity amid bearish sentiment and falling prices,【113† S&P Global Commodity Insights reported earlier†platform.platts.spglobal.com】. There have been very few inquiries from traders and scarce transactions, according to a Chinese producer.

"Overseas are cutting their orders because they cannot use up the amount they purchased under long-term contract," said a second Chinese producer.

However, soft market trends should be expected in the burgeoning lithium industry, and long-term fundamentals remain strong, according to Rahul Sen Sharma, president and co-CEO of Indxx.

"When you're talking about these big disruptive transformational changes, oftentimes you have problems and other types of issues that come up because you're trying to change so much so quickly," Sen Sharma told S&P Global. "This is normal, and I don't think it should be unexpected."

Indxx provides indexing solutions for ETFs and offers some products focused on the battery material sector.

Bullish sentiment for the lithium and battery sectors is also evident in Quebec, which has been investing heavily to establish the complete supply chain within the province, from mining to electric vehicle production.

"The demand will be there, whatever happens, because we need to electrify our cars," Jean-François Béland, vice president of Ressources Québec, said in an interview.

Ressources Québec, a unit of Investissement Québec (IQ), is working to foster investment in the province's energy and natural resources sectors.

"Lithium and critical minerals are, in the 21st century, what coal was in the 19th century and what oil was in the 20th century," Béland added.

### Incoming projects

Since 2020, the fallouts from the pandemic and various geopolitical events have strained international supply chains and led to record-high commodity prices. At the same time, governments globally have introduced waves of policy initiatives promoting energy transition, industrial onshoring and regional supply chains.

[Image 2: Global lithium market share and size, 2023]

Rechargeable lithium-polymer cells are used in cell phones, 【93†laptops】, toys, digital cameras, small and large appliances, tablets, e-readers, and power tools. These batteries are made from critical materials, such as cobalt, graphite, and lithium, and need to be handled with safety and precautions. Various developed countries are investing increasingly in the deployment of energy storage systems based on Li-ion batteries, thus fueling market growth.

For instance, the UK launched a 50-megawatt energy system connected to the high-voltage transmission system of its National Grid. This project is part of the USD 48.5 million Energy Superhub Oxford (ESO) plan for the country. Pivot Power is leading the project, which is backed by the Government of the UK.

## Regional Insights 

The lithium market in North America held a global revenue share of more than 13.0% in 2023. The government's increasing focus on reducing carbon emissions in the automotive sector is expected to propel market growth in the coming years.

[Image 3: Lithium Market Trends, by Region, 2024 - 2030]

### U.S. Lithium Market Trends

The U.S. lithium market is one of the largest consumers of lithium in North America. The market growth is attributed to positive government policies and initiatives on green energy transition, and EVs are propelling the demand for the product in the region.

### Asia Pacific Lithium Market Trends

Asia Pacific lithium market dominated globally with the largest revenue share of more than 52.0% in 2023, owing to rapidly developing automotive, glass, and consumer goods industries in countries such as China, Japan, and South Korea. The region will expand further, maintaining its dominance and growing at the fastest CAGR in terms of volume over the forecast period.

The China lithium market held a revenue share of approximately 57.0% in Asia Pacific in 2023. The rising focus on renewable energy and EV production is positively influencing the product market.

### Europe Lithium Market Trends

The lithium market in Europe held the second-largest share of global revenue in 2023 and is projected to witness steady growth from 2024 to 2030. The market's growth in Europe can be attributed to the region's increasing production of EVs.

The Germany lithium market held over 12.0% revenue share in the European region in 2023. The increasing government regulation is expected to propel the demand for the product in the country.

### Central & South America Lithium Market Trends

The lithium market in Central & South America held the least share of the global market. The availability of resources has spurred local mining activities and attracted foreign investments, boosting the lithium industry in the region.

## Key Lithium Company Insights

Market players compete against product quality, reliability in terms of supply and customer service, and diversity in product portfolio. Furthermore, market players are investing in battery sector, which is key application of lithium. For instance, in June 2021, Albemarle announced about opening of an Innovation Center at its site in Kings Mountain, North Carolina, U.S. The center will aid in supporting the company’s carbonate and hydroxide products, and advanced energy storage materials product portfolio.

Some of the key players operating in the market include Albemarle, Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd., and Mineral Resources.

  * Albemarle’s lithium segment is engaged in the development of lithium-based materials, which cater to a wide range of industries. The segment manufactures lithium carbonate, lithium hydroxide, lithium chloride, and value-added lithium specialties and reagents, including butyllithium and lithium aluminum hydride. In addition, the segment offers technical services such as handling reactive lithium products and customer recycling services for lithium-containing by-products that are obtained from synthesis with organolithium products, lithium metal, and other reagents.

  * Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd. serves a wide category of industries, including electric vehicles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, energy storage, and 3C (Computer, Communication, and Consumer Electronics) products. The company has capability to extract lithium from ore, brine, and recycled materials. The company offers more than 40 lithium and other metal compounds.

  * Mineral Resources provides mining services, including crushing, processing, port operation, supply-chain amenities, site services, shipping, and marketing. Mineral Resources has three joint-venture projects: the Mt Marion Lithium Project, the Marillana Iron Ore Project, and MARBL.

  * General Lithium Corporation, Sigma Lithium Resources, and Livent Corporation are some of the emerging market participants. General Lithium Corporation provides industrial-grade and battery-grade lithium carbonate, high-purity lithium carbonate, and lithium iron phosphate, among other products. The products are mainly for the battery industry.

  * Sigma Lithium Resources is a mineral production company focused on lithium projects in Brazil-based mines. The company is particularly interested in the globally expanding supply chain of electric vehicles.

  * Livent Corporation is a fully integrated lithium company that produces lithium compounds. Its key products include high-purity lithium metal, butyllithium, lithium carbonate, and battery-grade lithium hydroxide.

### Key Lithium Companies:

The following are the leading companies in the lithium market. These companies collectively hold the largest market share and dictate industry trends.

  * Albemarle Corp.
  * Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd.
  * SQM S.A.
  * Tianqi Lithium Corporation
  * Livent Corp.
  * Lithium Americas Corp.
  * Pilbara Minerals
  * Orocobre Limited Pty. Ltd.
  * Mineral Resources Group Co., Ltd.

## Recent Developments

  * In November 2023, ExxonMobil announced that work had commenced for its first lithium well drilling in Arkansas, an area with significant quantities of lithium deposits.

### By Application Analysis

Batteries to Hold Major Share owing to the Growing Demand from Consumer Electronics

On the basis of application, the market is segmented into batteries, glass & 【48†ceramics】, lubricant, polymers, metallurgy, medical, air treatment, and others.

The batteries segment accounted for a major market share in 2023 and will likely continue its dominance during the forecast timeframe. LIBs are used in many combinations of active materials for the cathode, electrolyte, and anode. They are either primary or secondary batteries. Primary batteries are used in cameras, calculators, electronic games, watches, computers, and other devices. In contrast, secondary batteries are used in portable computers, telephones, tablets, electric vehicles, cordless tools, and video cameras.

A surge in electric vehicle sales due to rise in per capita disposable income and user preferences will drive the LIB market. The demand for rechargeable batteries declined due to the coronavirus outbreak, thus contributing to the downfall of the automotive industry. As per the BloombergNEF forecast, battery consignments to carmakers fell by about 14% in 2020. Thus, consumer awareness and a major mind shift toward low-cost transportation will drive market growth in the coming years.

Metal carbonate is used to lower the temperature and thermal expansion in glass and ceramics applications. It is used in glass-ceramics cooktops to reduce thermal expansion, ensure color consistency, increase mold strength, improve durability, lower viscosity, and increase melt rate. SCHOTT AG specializes in manufacturing glass and glass-ceramics and uses a lithium aluminium silicate system to produce glass-ceramics, such as CERAN cooktop panels, ZERODUR glass-ceramic fire protection glasses and security, and ROBAX fire viewing windows for fireplaces.

To know how our report can help streamline your business, 【49† Speak to Analyst 】 

### By End-User Analysis

The Automotive Industry Dominates the Market Due to a Growing Preference for Hybrid and Electric Vehicles

On the basis of end-user, the market is segmented into automotive, 【50†consumer electronics】, industrial, energy storage, and others.

The automobile industry is currently dominated by fossil fuel consumption but is increasingly moving toward becoming an alternate source of energy, such as lithium-ion-backed battery technology. The increasing demand for EVs and the shift toward clean energy will drive the product demand in the coming years. For instance, the Indian Government launched FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles) along with national & state-level regulations to make 30% of electric cars target by 2030 by adding 450 GW of renewable sources by establishing 34 GW/136 GW of battery storage requirements to make the country a major user of LIB.

The consumer electronics segment has grown exponentially in recent times. LIBs are used under rechargeable gadgets to store the proper energy-to-weight ratios and high open-circuit voltage. The advancement in battery technology is making electronic products more refined and slim, which makes higher use of batteries to increase the running time of products. In addition, these batteries have a high power density for more battery life in a lighter package. Hence, an increase in demand for 【51†smartphones】 and consumer electronics is expected to drive market growth.

## REGIONAL INSIGHTS

Asia Pacific Lithium Market Size, 2023 (USD Billion)

To get more information on the regional analysis of this market, 【52† Request a Free sample 】 

Asia Pacific is estimated to hold the largest lithium market share, owing to widespread product usage in the industrial and commercial sectors, including power, consumer electronics, chemical, industrial, general manufacturing, and others. Asia Pacific is rapidly developing due to various government initiatives and increasing foreign investments in the industrial sector. The easy availability of raw materials is considered one factor supporting the market growth.

Additionally, the presence of a large number of lithium and its derivatives-producing companies in emerging countries such as India, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and China is surging the product demand. China is one of the largest producers of electronic components such as fuel cells, batteries, and capacitors. There has been advancement in fuel cell technologies for electric vehicles to aid the rules set by the government to reduce the pollution that occurs due to the burning of petrochemicals and gasoline.

The market in North America is likely to rise considerably during the lithium market forecast period. The increasing adoption of cleaner energy sources due to stringent regulatory rules is surging regional growth. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has various schemes and funding programs that support the usage of green and sustainable sources of energy like solar, wind, geothermal, and others. The increasing adoption of 【53†solar panels】 has created a substantial demand for cells and batteries to store energy.

For instance, in a technology transfer program of NASA, the gas-powered engines of aircraft were replaced by LIB packs designed by NASA and other contractor partnerships. These factors will contribute to the growth of the market in North America.

Europe has witnessed significant industrial development in the last decade. The increasing investment of the European Union for R&D in automobile, ICT, and healthcare sectors is the main factor driving the market growth. According to the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA), Europe's battery electric vehicles hold 12.1% of the total market share, compared to 9.1%in 2021 or 1.9%in 2019.

Latin America accounts for around 70% of the world’s lithium reserves, where the metal is used in rechargeable batteries for EVs and mobile phones. Chile produces metals that are cheap and high-quality. Chile’s government is allowing new entrants as the region's market is consolidated in nature.

### With COVID-19 in the rear-view mirror, how are in-person events supporting the battery industry?

Did you know there were over 100 lithium-related events last year? We launched a global lithium events calendar in 2023 to keep track of them all and shared it with our stakeholders on our website. This year, 【71†we are tracking even more events†lithium.org】, and you can add them all to your calendar with a click of the mouse!

It would have been a full-time job to attend all the lithium events last year, but we did manage to attend over 20 and give presentations at most of those. Our own events schedule grew nicely, too. We hosted in-person networking events in Salta, Argentina; Perth, Australia; London, United Kingdom; and Las Vegas, United States. This was in addition to our regular series of webinars exclusively for members covering the lithium market and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues.

### How has lithium demand evolved over the last 12 months? Are there any emerging trends, and are we on track to meet approaching climate targets?

The short answer is that lithium demand continued to show double-digit growth last year, driven by the transition to green transport. 【40†Electric vehicle (EV)】 sales in 2023 reached 【72†14 million units†www.ev-volumes.com】, representing 34% growth over 2022.

Like any significant industrial policy, the energy transition faces challenges; however, momentum is building, and regulatory support is growing.

The growing use of lithium batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) is also noteworthy. ESS play a key role in meeting net zero targets, storing energy from different sources and discharging it when needed. ESS help to balance the electric grid, provide backup power, and improve grid stability, which is important when an increasing percentage of electricity comes from intermittent renewable sources.

[Image 3]© shutterstock/Quality Stock Arts

### Are there any challenges in the supply chain for lithium batteries that have surfaced recently, and what steps are being taken to mitigate these challenges?

Education is a perennial challenge because of the rapid growth in the social and economic importance of lithium. As recently as five years ago, politicians rarely mentioned lithium, but now it has become a hot topic with all the media attention and regulatory interest this brings. We are seeing a real thirst for reliable information about lithium from industry, regulators, and the public.

On a more practical level, a key challenge is the time needed to bring on new industrial lithium mines. This is far longer than the time needed to build a refinery or EV factory, even up to ten years. We often hear from our members that the bottleneck is the time taken to secure permission, and it is encouraging to see several countries looking very closely at their legislative framework with regard to encouraging faster development of lithium mines without sacrificing the quality of the process.

### ILiA and its members all champion sustainability in the industry. Are there any emerging practices that are helping to ensure this further?

Yes, that is correct. In fact, sustainability is one of ILiA’s three core principles and was one of the key considerations for the founding members when they created ILiA in 2021. We support our members’ efforts to supply lithium that is sustainably and responsibly sourced through workshops, webinars, and the work of our technical subcommittees.

Many lithium companies are adopting standards that certify their performance. There are many mining standards which can apply to the lithium industry, and ILiA does not endorse a particular one, but it is worth recognising that last year, two of our Core Members, Albemarle Corporation and SQM, achieved the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) standard, which is considered by many people in the industry to be the hardest mining standard to achieve.

### What is ILiA working on to support its members in achieving sustainability?

One of our flagship projects, run by the Sustainable Lithium Subcommittee, is the creation of standardised guidance on how to measure the product environmental footprint of carbon and water used in lithium mining and refining. This will have a major impact, we hope, in streamlining how lithium life cycle assessments (LCAs) are done. The standardised guidance will be clear, concise, and accessible to producers, suppliers, LCA practitioners, authorities, and academia. Our goal is for lithium LCAs to truly represent the industry and contain reliable and comparable information.

It is of critical importance for the lithium industry as it will serve to create a benchmark by which the industry can measure its greenhouse gas credentials. It will be available on the ILiA website for download.

For this project, we created a global multi-stakeholder team of members and non-members under the leadership of Mark De Boer from Albemarle Corporation. The first chapter focuses on the carbon footprint of lithium and will be published in the first quarter of 2024. The second chapter will examine the water footprint of the lithium industry and will be published in the second half of 2024. Both projects are open to the public, and anyone interested in joining should contact us.

### What regulatory or policy changes have affected the lithium market in the past year, and how have industry players adapted to these changes?

The last year was something of a watershed for the lithium industry, with several major regulations and legislations hitting their stride. For example, in November 2023, the European Union reached a provisional agreement on the Critical Raw Materials Act, which aims to increase and diversify the EU’s critical raw materials supply, strengthen circularity and recycling and boost research and innovation on resource efficiency.

Another key theme in regulatory developments is battery recycling. The battery in an EV can be recycled repeatedly, creating a circular ec

US and Canadian lithium sector development could still forge ahead in 2024 with the potential startup of new construction projects to provide much-needed domestic supply, despite pricing and demand headwinds that weighed on the global industry this year.

###### Not registered?

Receive daily email alerts, subscriber notes & personalize your experience. 

【112† Register Now 】 

As 2023 ends, market participants in the key north Asia market are reporting ongoing weakness for spot lithium activity amid bearish sentiment and falling prices,【113† S&P Global Commodity Insights reported earlier†platform.platts.spglobal.com】. There have been very few inquiries from traders and scarce transactions, according to a Chinese producer.

"Overseas are cutting their orders because they cannot use up the amount they purchased under long-term contract," said a second Chinese producer.

However, soft market trends should be expected in the burgeoning lithium industry, and long-term fundamentals remain strong, according to Rahul Sen Sharma, president and co-CEO of Indxx.

"When you're talking about these big disruptive transformational changes, oftentimes you have problems and other types of issues that come up because you're trying to change so much so quickly," Sen Sharma told S&P Global. "This is normal, and I don't think it should be unexpected."

Indxx provides indexing solutions for ETFs and offers some products focused on the battery material sector.

Bullish sentiment for the lithium and battery sectors is also evident in Quebec, which has been investing heavily to establish the complete supply chain within the province, from mining to electric vehicle production.

"The demand will be there, whatever happens, because we need to electrify our cars," Jean-François Béland, vice president of Ressources Québec, said in an interview.

Ressources Québec, a unit of Investissement Québec (IQ), is working to foster investment in the province's energy and natural resources sectors.

"Lithium and critical minerals are, in the 21st century, what coal was in the 19th century and what oil was in the 20th century," Béland added.

### Incoming projects

Since 2020, the fallouts from the pandemic and various geopolitical events have strained international supply chains and led to record-high commodity prices. At the same time, governments globally have introduced waves of policy initiatives promoting energy transition, industrial onshoring and regional supply chains.

### Latest Trends and Developments in the Lithium Sector:

1. **Rising Demand for Electric Vehicles (EVs)**:
   - The electrification of transportation is a significant driver for lithium demand. EV sales continue to grow, with lithium-ion batteries being the preferred choice due to their high energy density and fast charging capabilities. The sector also includes electric buses, trucks, and other vehicles, contributing to reduced greenhouse gas emissions from transportation【21†source】【23†source】.

2. **Innovative Extraction Methods**:
   - Traditional lithium mining poses environmental challenges, prompting the development of sustainable extraction technologies. Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) is a promising method that reduces water usage and environmental impact while increasing efficiency. DLE can extract lithium from lower concentration brines more effectively, making it a cost-efficient and eco-friendly alternative【23†source】.

3. **Battery Technology Advancements**:
   - Continuous improvements in lithium-ion battery technology are essential for meeting the growing demand. Innovations include solid-state batteries, which offer higher energy density and improved safety, and new electrode materials that enhance battery performance. These advancements are critical for applications beyond EVs, such as renewable energy storage systems【23†source】.

4. **Renewable Energy Storage**:
   - Lithium-ion batteries play a crucial role in renewable energy storage, helping to stabilize grids by storing excess energy from sources like solar and wind power. Their high energy density, long lifespan, and fast charging capabilities make them ideal for grid-scale storage, behind-the-meter storage, and microgrids【23†source】.

5. **Regional Market Dynamics**:
   - The Asia-Pacific region dominates the lithium market, driven by rapidly developing automotive, glass, and consumer goods industries in countries like China, Japan, and South Korea. The region is expected to maintain its dominance and grow at the fastest rate. North America and Europe are also significant markets, with government policies promoting green energy transitions and EV adoption【21†source】【22†source】.

### Opportunities for You:

Given your background, here are some strategic steps you can take to benefit from these trends:

1. **Invest in Lithium Technology Development**:
   - Develop software solutions for optimizing lithium extraction and refining processes.
   - Innovate in battery management systems to enhance the performance and safety of lithium-ion batteries.

2. **Collaborate with Industry Leaders**:
   - Partner with global lithium companies to bring advanced extraction and processing technologies to India.
   - Engage in joint ventures and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

3. **Focus on Sustainable Practices**:
   - Promote and implement sustainable extraction methods like DLE.
   - Advocate for and ensure compliance with environmental standards in lithium mining projects.

4. **Explore Renewable Energy Storage Solutions**:
   - Develop and market lithium-ion battery solutions for renewable energy storage applications.
   - Invest in research and development of next-generation battery technologies, such as solid-state batteries.

By aligning with these trends and leveraging your skills, you can position yourself to take advantage of the growing opportunities in the lithium sector.

[Image 2: Global lithium market share and size, 2023]

Rechargeable lithium-polymer cells are used in cell phones, 【93†laptops】, toys, digital cameras, small and large appliances, tablets, e-readers, and power tools. These batteries are made from critical materials, such as cobalt, graphite, and lithium, and need to be handled with safety and precautions. Various developed countries are investing increasingly in the deployment of energy storage systems based on Li-ion batteries, thus fueling market growth.

For instance, the UK launched a 50-megawatt energy system connected to the high-voltage transmission system of its National Grid. This project is part of the USD 48.5 million Energy Superhub Oxford (ESO) plan for the country. Pivot Power is leading the project, which is backed by the Government of the UK.

## Regional Insights 

The lithium market in North America held a global revenue share of more than 13.0% in 2023. The government's increasing focus on reducing carbon emissions in the automotive sector is expected to propel market growth in the coming years.

[Image 3: Lithium Market Trends, by Region, 2024 - 2030]

### U.S. Lithium Market Trends

The U.S. lithium market is one of the largest consumers of lithium in North America. The market growth is attributed to positive government policies and initiatives on green energy transition, and EVs are propelling the demand for the product in the region.

### Asia Pacific Lithium Market Trends

Asia Pacific lithium market dominated globally with the largest revenue share of more than 52.0% in 2023, owing to rapidly developing automotive, glass, and consumer goods industries in countries such as China, Japan, and South Korea. The region will expand further, maintaining its dominance and growing at the fastest CAGR in terms of volume over the forecast period.

The China lithium market held a revenue share of approximately 57.0% in Asia Pacific in 2023. The rising focus on renewable energy and EV production is positively influencing the product market.

### Europe Lithium Market Trends

The lithium market in Europe held the second-largest share of global revenue in 2023 and is projected to witness steady growth from 2024 to 2030. The market's growth in Europe can be attributed to the region's increasing production of EVs.

The Germany lithium market held over 12.0% revenue share in the European region in 2023. The increasing government regulation is expected to propel the demand for the product in the country.

### Central & South America Lithium Market Trends

The lithium market in Central & South America held the least share of the global market. The availability of resources has spurred local mining activities and attracted foreign investments, boosting the lithium industry in the region.

## Key Lithium Company Insights

Market players compete against product quality, reliability in terms of supply and customer service, and diversity in product portfolio. Furthermore, market players are investing in battery sector, which is key application of lithium. For instance, in June 2021, Albemarle announced about opening of an Innovation Center at its site in Kings Mountain, North Carolina, U.S. The center will aid in supporting the company’s carbonate and hydroxide products, and advanced energy storage materials product portfolio.

Some of the key players operating in the market include Albemarle, Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd., and Mineral Resources.

  * Albemarle’s lithium segment is engaged in the development of lithium-based materials, which cater to a wide range of industries. The segment manufactures lithium carbonate, lithium hydroxide, lithium chloride, and value-added lithium specialties and reagents, including butyllithium and lithium aluminum hydride. In addition, the segment offers technical services such as handling reactive lithium products and customer recycling services for lithium-containing by-products that are obtained from synthesis with organolithium products, lithium metal, and other reagents.

  * Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd. serves a wide category of industries, including electric vehicles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, energy storage, and 3C (Computer, Communication, and Consumer Electronics) products. The company has capability to extract lithium from ore, brine, and recycled materials. The company offers more than 40 lithium and other metal compounds.

  * Mineral Resources provides mining services, including crushing, processing, port operation, supply-chain amenities, site services, shipping, and marketing. Mineral Resources has three joint-venture projects: the Mt Marion Lithium Project, the Marillana Iron Ore Project, and MARBL.

  * General Lithium Corporation, Sigma Lithium Resources, and Livent Corporation are some of the emerging market participants. General Lithium Corporation provides industrial-grade and battery-grade lithium carbonate, high-purity lithium carbonate, and lithium iron phosphate, among other products. The products are mainly for the battery industry.

  * Sigma Lithium Resources is a mineral production company focused on lithium projects in Brazil-based mines. The company is particularly interested in the globally expanding supply chain of electric vehicles.

  * Livent Corporation is a fully integrated lithium company that produces lithium compounds. Its key products include high-purity lithium metal, butyllithium, lithium carbonate, and battery-grade lithium hydroxide.

### Key Lithium Companies:

The following are the leading companies in the lithium market. These companies collectively hold the largest market share and dictate industry trends.

  * Albemarle Corp.
  * Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd.
  * SQM S.A.
  * Tianqi Lithium Corporation
  * Livent Corp.
  * Lithium Americas Corp.
  * Pilbara Minerals
  * Orocobre Limited Pty. Ltd.
  * Mineral Resources Group Co., Ltd.

## Recent Developments

  * In November 2023, ExxonMobil announced that work had commenced for its first lithium well drilling in Arkansas, an area with significant quantities of lithium deposits.

* The increasing electrification of transportation: In addition to EVs, lithium-ion batteries are also used in electric buses, trucks, and other vehicles. This is helping to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the transportation sector.

Overall, the future of lithium looks very bright. Lithium is a critical mineral in the transition to clean energy, and demand for lithium is expected to grow significantly in the coming years. Lithium Harvest is well-positioned to meet this growing demand with its sustainable lithium extraction solution.

【16† What is the best way to extract lithium? 】 

## Advancements in Lithium Extraction

Innovative extraction methods are essential to meet the increasing demand for lithium. Traditional mining practices pose environmental challenges, necessitating the development of sustainable alternatives. Lithium Harvest utilizes cutting-edge technology, such as 【17†Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE)】, to extract lithium efficiently and with minimal environmental impact. This breakthrough approach ensures a more sustainable and responsible future for lithium production.

DLE is a promising new technology that has the potential to revolutionize lithium extraction. It uses various methods, such as electrodialysis, ion exchange, and adsorption, to extract lithium ions directly from brine or other lithium-rich solutions. DLE offers several advantages over traditional mining practices, including:

  * Microgrids: Lithium-ion batteries can be used to create microgrids, which are self-sufficient energy systems that can operate independently of the main grid. This can be beneficial for areas prone to power outages or not connected to the grid.

## Regional Insights 

The lithium market in North America held a global revenue share of more than 13.0% in 2023. The government's increasing focus on reducing carbon emissions in the automotive sector is expected to propel market growth in the coming years.

[Image 3: Lithium Market Trends, by Region, 2024 - 2030]

### U.S. Lithium Market Trends

The U.S. lithium market is one of the largest consumers of lithium in North America. The market growth is attributed to positive government policies and initiatives on green energy transition, and EVs are propelling the demand for the product in the region.

### Asia Pacific Lithium Market Trends

Asia Pacific lithium market dominated globally with the largest revenue share of more than 52.0% in 2023, owing to rapidly developing automotive, glass, and consumer goods industries in countries such as China, Japan, and South Korea. The region will expand further, maintaining its dominance and growing at the fastest CAGR in terms of volume over the forecast period.

The China lithium market held a revenue share of approximately 57.0% in Asia Pacific in 2023. The rising focus on renewable energy and EV production is positively influencing the product market.

### Europe Lithium Market Trends

The lithium market in Europe held the second-largest share of global revenue in 2023 and is projected to witness steady growth from 2024 to 2030. The market's growth in Europe can be attributed to the region's increasing production of EVs.

The Germany lithium market held over 12.0% revenue share in the European region in 2023. The increasing government regulation is expected to propel the demand for the product in the country.

### Central & South America Lithium Market Trends

The lithium market in Central & South America held the least share of the global market. The availability of resources has spurred local mining activities and attracted foreign investments, boosting the lithium industry in the region.

## Key Lithium Company Insights

Market players compete against product quality, reliability in terms of supply and customer service, and diversity in product portfolio. Furthermore, market players are investing in battery sector, which is key application of lithium. For instance, in June 2021, Albemarle announced about opening of an Innovation Center at its site in Kings Mountain, North Carolina, U.S. The center will aid in supporting the company’s carbonate and hydroxide products, and advanced energy storage materials product portfolio.

Some of the key players operating in the market include Albemarle, Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd., and Mineral Resources.

  * Albemarle’s lithium segment is engaged in the development of lithium-based materials, which cater to a wide range of industries. The segment manufactures lithium carbonate, lithium hydroxide, lithium chloride, and value-added lithium specialties and reagents, including butyllithium and lithium aluminum hydride. In addition, the segment offers technical services such as handling reactive lithium products and customer recycling services for lithium-containing by-products that are obtained from synthesis with organolithium products, lithium metal, and other reagents.

  * Ganfeng Lithium Co., Ltd. serves a wide category of industries, including electric vehicles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, energy storage, and 3C (Computer, Communication, and Consumer Electronics) products. The company has capability to extract lithium from ore, brine, and recycled materials. The company offers more than 40 lithium and other metal compounds.

  * Mineral Resources provides mining services, including crushing, processing, port operation, supply-chain amenities, site services, shipping, and marketing. Mineral Resources has three joint-venture projects: the Mt Marion Lithium Project, the Marillana Iron Ore Project, and MARBL.

  * General Lithium Corporation, Sigma Lithium Resources, and Livent Corporation are some of the emerging market participants. General Lithium Corporation provides industrial-grade and battery-grade lithium carbonate, high-purity lithium carbonate, and lithium iron phosphate, among other products. The products are mainly for the battery industry.

  * Sigma Lithium Resources is a mineral production company focused on lithium projects in Brazil-based mines. The company is particularly interested in the globally expanding supply chain of electric vehicles.

  * Livent Corporation is a fully integrated lithium company that produces lithium compounds. Its key products include high-purity lithium metal, butyllithium, lithium carbonate, and battery-grade lithium hydroxide.
